text:
anya: quick spike results from the 'heap-paint + thin-slab' allocator experiment. sending raw notes here for visibility.

devon: nice, curious — what's the hypothesis again?

anya: hypothesis: allocate short-lived decode buffers from a thin-slab overlay (narrow per-request micro-slab) and reserve a small 'painted' region for hot KV prefill blocks to reduce fragmentation and avoid large free-list churn. should reduce OOMs when mix of long-lived KV + bursty prefills.

max: what metrics did you measure? tails matter.

anya: measured: 95/99/99.9 token-latency, OOM count, slab-fragmentation ratio (free bytes / total bytes per slab), and successful prefill hit-rate. also kernel-selection changes because we forced smaller workspace per kernel.

anya: raw numbers (baseline vs paint+thin):
```
baseline: 95=27ms, 99=54ms, 99.9=183ms, OOMs=18/hr, frag=0.42, prefill-hit=0.73
paint+thin: 95=29ms, 99=60ms, 99.9=210ms, OOMs=3/hr, frag=0.18, prefill-hit=0.88
```

devon: OOMs dropping to 3/hr is huge. but tails got worse — any idea why 99.9 increased?

anya: two drivers: (1) when thin-slab is exhausted on a busy GPU, we fall back to allocating a larger workspace from the global heap which triggers a kernel that forces a synchronous migration path (scheduling spike), (2) a few requests hit kernel-selection fallback that picks the slower attention kernel for the small workspace scenario.

max: so tradeoff: fewer OOMs, better fragmentation, but worse extreme tails due to fallback behavior. Can we avoid the synchronous fallback?

anya: plan: (A) add a soft-reserve for thin-slab that can be temporarily enlarged by borrowing from LRU-painted region up to X% to avoid the synchronous path; (B) tweak kernel selector to prefer the fast-kernel variant when workspace slightly under target if qkv dims permit.

devon: A sounds fine. For B, we need microbenchmarks — do we have a quick script?

anya: ran microbench: `./bench/kernel-select --seq 512 --bs 8 --workspace 75%` shows fast-kernel still wins for 80% of seeds but not for pathological head counts. Will paste CI perf map soon.

runtime-bot: deploy: allocator-paint-v1 rolled to canary (3 hosts) at 2024-11-08T15:04Z.

sre-ops: noticed a canary with long decode spike ~15:07Z, pid=4219; logs show fallback allocation path taken twice in 10s. Captured heap traces attached in S3: s3://redwood-telemetry/alloc-traces/3072001234-4219.log

anya: thanks — I'll add a debounce window on the borrow path to stop oscillation. also going to add a metric: `thin_slab_borrow_count` and `kernel_fallback_count`.

devon: do we want per-request caps (hard) to stop a single request from draining thin-slab?

anya: we already tested per-request soft caps (reject borrow unless usage < cap). soft caps kept tail low but lowered prefill-hit. tradeoffs: availability vs efficiency. proposing adaptive soft caps: tighten when borrow_count > threshold.

max: sounds reasonable. can you sketch rollout?

anya: rollout plan: canary (3 hosts) -> expand to 20% with borrow debounce & `thin_slab_borrow_limit=0.12` -> monitor metrics for 6h windows (oom_count, 99.9 latency, borrow_count) -> if 99.9>baseline+20% revert. I'll open a short PR with flags and perf dashboard.

devon: please include synthetic stress test that mixes long-lived KV inserts + bursty prefill (50% traffic) for 30m. we saw latent regressions only under mixed workloads.

anya: done locally, running on perf harness now. linking artifacts in thread once complete. :eyes:
